{"metadata":{"description":"DeepSeek Harness plugin that blocks agent edits that weaken tests, such as .skip, deleted or watered-down assertions.","id":"gh:1420637154","install_available":true,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-protect-tests","slug":"acus9345/dsh-protect-tests","topics":["ai-agents","coding-agent","deepseek-harness","dsh-plugin","testing"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"DeepSeek Harness plugin that blocks agent edits that weaken tests, such as .skip, deleted or watered"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"plugin that blocks agent edits that weaken tests, such as .skip, deleted or watered-down assertions."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-protect-tests"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"Tell an agent "make the tests pass" and sometimes it does exactly that, just not the way you meant. "},{"id":"p4s2","text":"A failing test gets `.skip`. An assertion gets commented out. `expect(total).toBe(42)` turns into `e"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"xpect(total).toBeDefined()`. The run goes green and the bug is still there."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"This DeepSeek Harness plugin looks at every edit to a test file before it's applied, comparing the o"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"ld text with the new. If the change makes the tests check less, the edit is refused and the model is"},{"id":"p5s3","text":" told what it did:
(haha claude is so useful i mean like idk)"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin"},{"id":"p9s3","text":" list, so add it to every profile you use. It's on as soon as it's installed. Remove it with `dsh pl"},{"id":"p9s4","text":"ugin --profile web remove dsh-protect-tests`."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"### From a clone"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"## What it notices"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"- **New skips.** `it.skip`, `test.only`, `xit`, `xdescribe`, `@pytest.mark.skip` / `xfail`, `@unitte"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"st.skip`, `t.Skip()`, `@Disabled`, `#[ignore]`, and the equivalents in xUnit, RSpec, PHPUnit and XCT"},{"id":"p14s3","text":"est.
- **Fewer tests or assertions.** Removing a test case, or removing two or more assertions in on"},{"id":"p14s4","text":"e edit. Both thresholds are configurable.
- **Assertions that can't fail.** `expect(true).toBe(true)"},{"id":"p14s5","text":"`, `assert True`, `assertEquals(x, x)`, `assert!(true)`.
- **Commented-out assertions.**
- **Swallow"},{"id":"p14s6","text":"ed failures.** Wrapping assertions in an empty `catch {}` or `except AssertionError: pass`.
- **Weak"},{"id":"p14s7","text":"er assertions.** Swapping a specific check for `toBeDefined()`, `toBeTruthy()`, `assert.ok(x)`, `is "},{"id":"p14s8","text":"not None` and the like.
- **Deleted test files.** `rm`, `git rm` or `unlink` on a test file or test "},{"id":"p14s9","text":"folder from the shell.
- **A test script that can't fail.** Changing `"test"` in `package.json` to `"},{"id":"p14s10","text":"echo`, `exit 0`, `... || true`, or adding `--passWithNoTests`."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"On Windows, PowerShell deletes (`Remove-Item`, `del`, `rd`) count too."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Test files are found by name: `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*_test.*`, `test_*.py`, `*Test.java`, `confte"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"st.py`, anything under `tests/`, `__tests__/`, `spec/` or `e2e/`, and so on. You can change the list"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"t.py`, anything under `tests/`, `__tests__/`, `spec/` or `e2e/`, and so on. You can change the list."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"Normal test work isn't affected. Adding tests, adding assertions, renaming, refactoring setup code a"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"nd fixing a typo in a test name all go through without a word. Refactors that look like losses on pa"},{"id":"p17s3","text":"per also go through, for example folding five near-identical tests into one `test.each` / `@pytest.m"},{"id":"p17s4","text":"ark.parametrize` / `t.Run` table, or merging three `toBe` checks into one `toEqual({...})` or a help"},{"id":"p17s5","text":"er like `expectUser(...)`."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"## When the test really is wrong"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"Sometimes it is. The requirement changed, or the test was asserting the bug. In that case the model "},{"id":"p19s2","text":"is asked to tell you which test it's changing and why, then repeat the same call once to confirm. Th"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"e repeat goes through. So the guard never fully blocks legitimate work. It just won't let a weakened"},{"id":"p19s4","text":" test slip past without being mentioned in the conversation. If you'd rather approve these yourself,"},{"id":"p19s5","text":"ithout being mentioned in the conversation. If you'd rather approve these yourself, use `mode: ask`."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"## What it won't catch"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"It works on patterns, not on meaning. If the model changes `toBe(4)` to `toBe(5)` to match a wrong r"},{"id":"p21s2","text":"esult, that looks like an ordinary edit and gets through. Rewriting the logic of a test so it no lon"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"ger exercises the bug also gets through. It covers the lazy shortcuts, which turn out to be most of "},{"id":"p21s4","text":"them, but it's no substitute for reading the diff."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"## Settings"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-protect-tests**, change what you want a"},{"id":"p23s2","text":"nd press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"Or add a row like this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or to `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.y"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"ml` for every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"## Development"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"The install test runs `dsh plugin add`, which needs `pnpm` on your PATH."},{"id":"p29s1","text":"MIT licensed. Written by acus9345. Bug reports and ideas are welcome in the issues."}],"truncated":false}
